brief.name: Illustrative case-flow modernization proposal
brief.audience: Operations sponsor, product leader, enterprise architect, security lead, and program steering committee
brief.decision: Authorize a four-week discovery and first-release definition phase, subject to access readiness and agreement on acceptance measures; later delivery remains a planning scenario, not a committed date or fee.

source_packet.role: fictional qualification brief; sole content source

slides.takeaway: A governed first journey makes the initial investment reviewable while preserving existing processing systems.
slides.assertion_title: One observable end-to-end journey is the right first investment
required_detail: Authorize a four-week discovery and first-release definition phase.
Make authorization conditional on access readiness and agreed acceptance measures.
Use the first release to make one end-to-end journey observable and governable.
Keep existing processing systems available during the first release.
Replacing only the portal would leave exceptions, duplicate case state, and difficult audit reconstruction.
The organization and operating conditions are synthetic.
No fee or remaining-program date is committed.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/phrase-highlight. This phrase-anchor accent-only fixture is an opening study, not a sufficient final argument page; root must enhance the dense argument template before final showcase. Keep the decision request and qualification adjacent to the anchored phrase.
qualifications: Fictional qualification scenario; not an actual client opportunity or West Monroe result.
Only the four-week discovery/definition decision is requested; subsequent timing and commercial terms are not committed.

slides.takeaway: Distributed status ownership creates handoffs and weak audit reconstruction across one service journey.
slides.assertion_title: Fragmented case ownership makes service friction hard to see and govern
required_detail: The fictional organization handles 18,000 service cases each month.
Cases enter through a portal, a shared operations queue, and three downstream processing systems.
Four teams exchange status updates in spreadsheets.
A synthetic baseline sample suggests 22% of cases need a manual handoff.
The sample suggests 14% arrive without enough information for first-pass processing.
Discovery must confirm definitions, sample coverage, and ownership before business-case use.
Replacing the portal alone leaves manual exceptions, duplicate case state, and difficult audit reconstruction.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/workflow-matrix. Use current constraints, proposed operating response, and measures to validate as linked columns.
qualifications: All volumes and baseline observations are synthetic assumptions.
Do not present 22% or 14% as validated performance facts or a business case.

slides.audience: Operations sponsor, product leader, and security lead
slides.takeaway: Five connected operating needs shape the first release and its acceptance measures.
slides.assertion_title: The first release must join intake, ownership, integration, evidence, and change
required_detail: Reliable intake: validate minimum information, establish a consistent case identifier, expose missing information, and preserve alternate intake routes during transition.
Clear ownership: assign a business owner, service queue, and escalation path to each case state; record decisions and reassignment reasons.
Controlled integration: use versioned interfaces and event contracts, starting with one supported integration; do not assume real-time support from every legacy interface.
Evidence for operations: link status, access, and processing events to an auditable case history; distinguish incomplete intake, waiting decisions, technical failures, and genuine demand.
Sustainable change: transfer runbooks, service ownership, release controls, and improvement routines; agree support responsibilities before first production release.
Measure completeness and first-touch rework using agreed definitions.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/needs-response. Preserve five paired need and response rows, with measures and control evidence tied to the relevant response.
qualifications: These are proposed requirements, not evidence of implemented capability.
One supported integration is the starting assumption; wider interface support requires validation.

slides.takeaway: A single case identifier and explicit state ownership connect intake, decisions, processing, and recovery.
slides.assertion_title: A traceable case journey can reduce ambiguity without merging systems
required_detail: Represent requester portal, shared operations queue, and three downstream processing systems as distinct participants.
Show intake validation and missing-information return path while alternate intake remains available during transition.
Assign business owner, service queue, and escalation route at each case state; capture decision and reassignment reasons.
Use the consistent case identifier to link status, access, processing events, and audit history.
Show technical failure, waiting decision, incomplete intake, and genuine demand as distinct exception categories.
Preserve transaction ownership in existing processing systems until an explicit migration decision.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/workflow-matrix. Use journey stages as rows and connect current friction, proposed owner/control, and evidence to validate; show exception states as row detail rather than a third process path.
qualifications: Journey details and operating assumptions require discovery validation.
The case identifier and event trace are proposed design responsibilities, not a committed vendor or platform selection.

slides.takeaway: A five-phase sequence moves from access readiness through proof and gated transition.
slides.assertion_title: Five gated phases establish the evidence before each expansion decision
required_detail: Mobilize before engagement: confirm sponsors, owners, data access, sample availability, security contacts, and first journey hypothesis.
Discover and define, weeks 1–4: observe the journey, validate baseline, map system constraints, define a thin release, and agree acceptance measures.
Build and prove, weeks 5–10: implement the first journey, interface contract, access controls, telemetry, and test evidence in a nonproduction environment.
Pilot and adapt, weeks 11–14: run a bounded cohort, rehearse exception handling, compare measures to validated baseline, and resolve readiness findings.
Scale and transition, weeks 15–20: expand only after steering gate, transfer operational ownership, and prioritize the next journey from measured evidence.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/five-phase. Give each phase its timing, activities, evidence output, and progression condition.
qualifications: All timing is illustrative and subject to access delays, source-data remediation, vendor constraints, and material control changes.
Additional journeys, integrations, and operating hours require separate scope decisions.

slides.audience: Sponsor, product leader, and delivery counterparts
slides.takeaway: Discovery converts an unvalidated baseline and broad problem into an owned thin-release definition.
slides.assertion_title: Discovery must validate the baseline before it defines acceptance
required_detail: Observe the first journey and map state ownership, handoffs, decisions, and exception paths.
Confirm definitions, sample coverage, and ownership for the assumed 22% manual-handoff and 14% incomplete-intake measures.
Map system constraints and dependencies, including the limits of legacy real-time support.
Define the thin release, first supported integration, control needs, and acceptance measures.
Produce validated baseline and sampling notes; journey and ownership map; interface and dependency register; prioritized thin-release backlog; and agreed control and acceptance checklist.
Any original UHG sample thumbnails shown on a phase-detail page are attributed design examples only, not deliverables produced for this fictional engagement.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/phase-detail. Pair objective, activity, evidence, and scope with attributed sample-artifact previews in a distinct design-reference zone.
qualifications: Discovery outputs are proposed deliverables for the fictional scenario.
Sample thumbnails, if used, must retain source attribution and must not be represented as project work product.

slides.takeaway: Layered responsibilities connect the journey while transaction ownership stays in existing systems.
slides.assertion_title: A governed integration layer can connect the journey without forcing consolidation
required_detail: Experience layer covers the requester portal, agent workspace, and supervisor decisions.
Orchestration layer covers case state and rules, exception routing, and integration events.
Platform layer covers identity and access, case data and audit, telemetry, and support.
The governance band defines product ownership, data stewardship, and change gates.
The security band spans identity, least privilege, data retention, and monitoring.
Keep transaction ownership in existing processing systems until an explicit migration decision.
Avoid an additional ungoverned copy of case state.
A canonical identifier and published event contracts connect the journey without requiring one platform in the first release.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/layered-architecture. Use its three layers and nine nodes with governance and security bands; do not add a standalone external-systems node.
qualifications: These are proposed responsibilities, not a prescribed vendor product stack.
Existing systems remain transaction owners; the diagram does not imply consolidation.
Interface feasibility, data authority, retention rules, and control design require client review.

slides.takeaway: Case intake and change approval move in parallel through clear owners, evidence, and explicit decisions.
slides.assertion_title: Case decisions and release changes need two governed review paths
required_detail: The case path validates intake and establishes the consistent case identifier.
It assigns a business owner and service queue before a case-state decision.
It routes exceptions to an explicit escalation path and records reassignment reasons.
The change path logs a proposed change and brings architecture and control owners into review.
It requires test evidence and operational readiness review before the steering release gate.
Release, hold, rollback, and recovery responsibilities must be explicit.
The architecture lead owns interface and control decisions with the client enterprise architect.
The program lead coordinates cross-team dependencies.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/parallel-process. The two sequenced paths are case intake/decision and change/release review; their control points converge at an explicit steering decision.
qualifications: The two paths describe proposed governance, not a committed tool or workflow implementation.
A supported interface and operating control details require discovery.

slides.takeaway: Readiness evidence and recovery decisions control when the program advances.
slides.assertion_title: The roadmap advances only when evidence and operational readiness support it
required_detail: Mobilization readiness depends on sponsors, owners, data access, sample availability, security contacts, and a first journey hypothesis.
Discovery and definition occupy illustrative weeks 1–4; build and prove weeks 5–10; pilot and adapt weeks 11–14; scale and transition weeks 15–20.
Access delays, unremediated source data, vendor constraints, or material control changes can move the sequence.
Additional journeys, integrations, and operating hours require separate scope decisions.
Proceed to pilot only after owners accept test evidence, critical control findings are resolved, operations can execute runbooks, and rollback is rehearsed.
Proceed to expansion only when validated baseline and pilot data support the decision; if evidence is weak or conditions change, adjust scope and retain the existing service.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/release-roadmap. Align phase ribbons to dependencies, owners, evidence, and proceed/hold/adjust gates.
qualifications: Timeline is illustrative, not a committed delivery date.
No expansion decision is implied before evidence and readiness gates are met.

slides.audience: Sponsor, steering committee, and client counterparts
slides.takeaway: Decision ownership is explicit across sponsorship, program coordination, architecture, pods, and client counterparts.
slides.assertion_title: Named responsibilities and client decision rights anchor the delivery model
required_detail: Sponsor and steering committee own investment and scope gates.
Program lead coordinates cross-team dependencies.
Architecture lead owns interface and control decisions with the client enterprise architect.
Three delivery pods cover journey experience, integration, and platform enablement.
Each pod has a lead and bounded mix of engineering, analysis, and quality roles.
Shared security, data, change, and service specialists participate at defined gates.
The 21-role organization diagram represents responsibilities and reporting relationships, not 21 full-time people.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/delivery-team. Show steering and program ownership, architecture accountability, delivery pods, shared capabilities, and client decision rights.
qualifications: The diagram is a responsibility model, not an FTE count or named staffing commitment.
Client role availability and decision rights need confirmation during mobilization.

slides.role: Roster cardinality and proposed lead profile
slides.takeaway: Nineteen role tiles describe coverage while allocation and availability remain open.
slides.assertion_title: The roster defines role categories, not a staffing total
required_detail: The roster has 19 tiles across core and specialist role categories.
The tiles are not an additive staffing total.
Allocation, named individuals, availability, rates, and delivery calendar require a separate staffing agreement.
The separate 21-role organization diagram represents responsibilities and reporting relationships, not 21 full-time people.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/dense-roster. Keep core and specialist categories distinct and label every tile as an illustrative role category.
qualifications: No named people or real credentials are supplied.
Role tiles do not imply full-time equivalents or total staffing.

slides.takeaway: A proposed platform delivery lead coordinates discovery, decisions, dependencies, and acceptance preparation.
slides.assertion_title: The proposed lead role coordinates evidence and decisions across the journey
required_detail: The profile describes a proposed platform delivery lead for a fictional case-flow modernization.
The role maps handoffs and decision points with service and technology owners.
It maintains decision and dependency records and translates agreed workflow rules into testable acceptance criteria.
It coordinates review with operations, architecture, security, and product stakeholders.
Proposed work areas include intake validation, case evidence traceability, exception routing, managed interfaces, recovery, and baseline ownership.
The role would help define a narrow pilot workflow and identify the systems and owners involved.
The team would prepare process maps, decision records, interface questions, and acceptance criteria for review.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/biography. Use a synthetic identity panel, role focus, working approach, three concise narrative zones, work areas, and proposed responsibilities.
qualifications: This page does not represent a real person or claim an actual credential.
Measures are proposed for validation, not reported outcomes.
Scope and sequence require discovery, data access, policy review, and delivery-capacity confirmation.

slides.takeaway: Pilot evidence—not activity completion—determines whether to proceed, adjust, or hold.
slides.assertion_title: Release decisions depend on validated measures, controls, runbooks, and recovery
required_detail: Discovery produces validated baseline and sampling notes.
It also produces a journey and ownership map, interface and dependency register, prioritized thin-release backlog, and agreed control and acceptance checklist.
Pilot measures include intake completeness, manual handoffs, decision latency, rework, and recoverability.
Candidate targets are manual handoffs from the assumed 22% toward 12%, incomplete intake from the assumed 14% toward 7%, and at least 95% traceability to an owner and timestamp.
The candidate targets are directional hypotheses, not performance commitments.
Proceed to pilot only after owners accept test evidence, critical control findings are resolved, operations can run the runbooks, and rollback is rehearsed.
Proceed to expansion only when validated baseline and pilot data support the decision.
If evidence is weak or conditions change, adjust scope and retain the existing service.
Do not declare success from activity completion alone.
slides.visual_relationship: Candidate family: wm/workflow-matrix. Use evidence, owner, measure, and decision columns for discovery outputs and pilot proceed/hold/adjust criteria.
qualifications: Target values require agreed definitions and validated baseline data.
The discovery baseline is assumed, not independently validated.

claims.assertion: The fictional operating context is 18,000 cases monthly, 22% assumed manual handoffs, and 14% assumed incomplete intake.
claims.qualification: Synthetic baseline sample only; not independently validated.

claims.assertion: Candidate pilot targets are 12% manual handoffs, 7% incomplete intake, and 95% traceability.
claims.qualification: Directional hypotheses only; not commitments, require agreed definitions and validated baseline.

claims.assertion: The proposed sequence extends from mobilization through scale and transition in illustrative weeks 1–20.
claims.qualification: Planning scenario; access, data, vendors, and control changes may move timing.
